newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: IEA CUTS BRAZIL OIL SUPPLY, RAISES DEMAND ESTIMATE. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IEA CUTS BRAZIL OIL SUPPLY, RAISES DEMAND ESTIMATE. [CORRECTED 19:55 GMT]

text.p: Brazil imported over one million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and refined products in May and demand growth went into double digits in June, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly oil report on Friday (corrects to make clear that the imports were of crude oil as well as refined products).
And while demand grows unexpectedly fast, extra supply is taking longer to appear than predicted.

The West's energy watchdog agency said it revised upwards by 100,000 bpd its Latin American second quarter 1997 demand figures to cater to Brazil's galloping pace of demand, and it cut its 1998 Brazil production forecast by 130,000 bpd.

"Brazilian demand is now estimated to have increased by a greater amount than previously anticipated... Preliminary data for Brazilian demand in June... indicate demand growth of 10.6 percent," the Paris-based agency said.
In May, Brazil consumed 1.94 million bpd, versus production of 897,000 bpd, the agency said.
Following a communication from state oil company Petrobras, the IEA revised downwards by 130,000 bpd its forecast of average output in 1998 to 1.07 million bpd.
